title: third-party-dep-risk-heatmap-and-evidence-runbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc combines a compact risk heatmap for third-party dependencies with a practical runbook for ingesting scanner output into our evidence store and pushing events to the SIEM. Goal is to reduce manual triage, enforce patch SLAs, and make remediation auditable by linking scanner proofs to ticket evidence artifacts.

Scope:
- Container and pip/npm/maven dependency results from internal CI and periodic SCA scans
- Evidence automation for remediation (artifacts pushed to S3 + SIEM event + ticket comment)
- RBAC notes for who can change remediation state (RBAC v2 brief)

Quick summary (last full run):
- Scan date: 2026-06-28 04:12 UTC
- Scanners: Trivy 0.39.0 (images), Snyk SCA scan (node/python/java), OSS Audit pipeline (sbom-based diff)
- Total findings: 348 (Critical: 6, High: 43, Medium: 129, Low: 170)
- Remediation backlog (open > SLA): 18 findings (7 high, 11 medium)

Risk heatmap (by component criticality x vuln severity) - ASCII view:

Component criticality -> Core infra | Customer-facing | Internal tooling | Research
Severity buckets down -> Critical | High | Medium | Low
Core infra                | 3 / 5 / 12 / 40
Customer-facing          | 2 / 18 / 50 / 88
Internal tooling         | 0 / 8 / 40 / 30
Research                 | 1 / 12 / 27 / 12

Notes: numbers are counts of findings in each cell. We prioritize Core infra Critical/High first, then Customer-facing, then others.

Representative scanner output snippets (sanitized):
- 2026-06-28T03:45:22Z | trivy:image | registry.redwood-internal/api:v2.1.4 | CVE-2024-2101 | HIGH | CVSS:8.1 | fix: bump to api:v2.1.6 | exploit: public PoC
- 2026-06-28T03:47:10Z | snyk:node | webapp/frontend@sha256:.. | SNYK-JS-LODASH-12345 | MEDIUM | path: package-lock.json | fix: lodash@4.17.21
- 2026-06-28T03:49:00Z | sbom-diff | service/analytics | GHSA-xxxx-yyyy | CRITICAL | note: vulnerable native lib, upgrade required to 2.0.0+

Remediation SLAs (proposed, actionable):
- Critical (exploit in wild, active exploitability or RCE in infra): remediate or mitigate in 48 hours. Temporary mitigations allowed with compensating controls.
- High (high severity, exploitable but limited conditions): remediate in 7 calendar days.
- Medium (low exploitability, non-prod exposure): remediate in 30 calendar days or schedule next maintenance window.
- Low: triage and track; no enforced SLA but must be reviewed quarterly.

Exception workflow:
- Ticket owner requests SLA extension via comment with justification + compensating control description. Security PM or SRE lead must approve by adding label "sla-exception-approved" on the Jira ticket. Approval must include expected remediation date.

Remediation tracking template (to append to Jira ticket comments and evidence store):
- scanner_run_id: <scanner-session-uuid>
- finding_id: <scanner finding id or CVE/GHSA>
- component: <service or image name>
- severity: <Critical/High/Medium/Low>
- fix: <PR/upgrade path or mitigation steps>
- proof_of_fix: <s3://evidence/vuln/2026-06-28/patch-PR-123.diff> (artifact URL)
- verification_log: <s3://evidence/vuln/2026-06-30/retest-output.json>
- remediation_owner: <team-person-email>
- rbac_closer_role: <sec-engineer|infra-owner|product-owner>

Automation playbook (high level):
1) CI publishes SBOM and SCA scan artifacts to artifacts/redwood-scans/<build-id>/
2) Post-scan lambda (scan-ingest-service) parses results and normalizes to our schema:
   - normalize fields: scanner, finding_id, cve, component, version, severity, cvss, fix_suggestion, evidence_uri
3) Normalizer writes raw artifact to S3 and posts normalized event to "vuln-ingest" Kafka topic
4) Ingest consumers:
   - evidence-linker: creates evidence object in evidence-store and attaches S3 URI
   - ticket-opener: creates or updates Jira (SEC-*) and appends remediation template + SLA metadata
   - siem-forwarder: converts normalized event into SIEM JSON and forwards to our SIEM via HTTPS with API key

SIEM export schema (fields we send) - example CSV header for export pipeline:
"event_time,event_id,source,component,component_version,scanner,finding_id,cve,cvss,severity,exploitability,fix_url,evidence_url,assigned_team,ticket_id"
Example SIEM JSON (single line):
{ "event_time": "2026-06-28T03:45:22Z", "event_id": "ingest-20260628-0001", "source": "trivy", "component": "api", "component_version": "v2.1.4", "scanner": "trivy", "finding_id": "CVE-2024-2101", "cve": "CVE-2024-2101", "cvss": "8.1", "severity": "HIGH", "exploitability": "public-poc", "fix_url": "https://github.com/redwood/api/pull/2107", "evidence_url": "s3://evidence/vuln/...", "assigned_team": "eng-platform", "ticket_id": "SEC-4821" }

Mapping to SIEM fields:
- evidence_url -> siem.dynamic_fields.artifact_uri
- assigned_team -> siem.tags.team
- finding_id/cve -> siem.rule.title
- cvss -> siem.risk.score (float)

RBAC v2 notes (who can mark remediation closed):
- Roles able to set ticket status to REMEDIATED: sec-engineer (security team), infra-owner (service owner), product-owner (service PO).
- Evidence upload permission: role "evidence-uploader" or service account used by ingest pipeline. Manual evidence edits require "evidence-editor" role.
- Audit requirement: any status change must generate an audit log entry with fields {actor, actor_role, action, target_ticket, timestamp, evidence_uri}. Audit log should be stored in append-only bucket with object lifecycle 7 years.

Verification checklist (manual or automated) before closing a ticket:
- [ ] Fix PR merged and deployed to all affected clusters (list deploy ids)
- [ ] Automated re-scan shows vulnerability absent in production images (attach verification_log)
- [ ] Evidence artifact uploaded and linked in ticket (proof_of_fix)
- [ ] SIEM event with remediation flag emitted OR ticket comment contains SIEM correlation id
- [ ] SLA met or exception approved

Playbook shortcuts and commands (ops notes):
- Re-run trivy on image: trivy image --format json --output /tmp/trivy-out.json registry.redwood-internal/api:v2.1.6
- Convert SBOM to SPDX: sbom-tool convert --in build.sbom.json --out build.spdx
- Manually push evidence to S3: aws s3 cp /tmp/retest-output.json s3://evidence/vuln/2026-06-30/retest-output.json --acl bucket-owner-full-control

Open questions / followups:
- Can SIEM enrichment include recent exploit telemetry (Threat Intel API) before auto-assigning Critical? (action: security-research to prototype)
- Should we require signed attestations for evidence artifacts from deployer service? (action: infra-security to evaluate feasibility)

Appendix: Helpful links
- Runbook: CONFLUENCE:sec/vuln-runbook-2026
- Jira epic for automation: JIRA:SEC-4800
- SBOM generator: GITHUB:tools/sbom-generator

Author note: This is intended to be practical and imperfect—please add concrete scripts or PR links as you implement automation steps. The priority is to reduce time-to-evidence so security can verify fixes within SLA without blocking engineering velocity.
